text:
alex: quick follow-up to the fairness scheduler RFC — need a short design call on where latency-aware quota routing should live. proposal sketch below. looking for objections or glaring issues before i write the PR.

maya: +1 to getting this nailed. TL;DR: enforce hard per-tenant quotas at ingress for correctness, but optimize routing decisions (latency vs cost) in the serving layer. why? fast denies need O(1) checks, routing can be heavier and approximate.

john: curious about bursts: if ingress does hard denies, how do we support transient burst tokens (e.g., short traffic spikes) without a global lock?

alex: good question. my idea: lease-based burst tokens handed out by the quota service with a short TTL (1-2s). ingress checks local cache first (optimistic), then a sync to quota service when cache miss or low reserve. so common-case is local and fast, worst-case hits quota service.

lee: worried about race conditions when multiple frontends allocate the same burst tokens concurrently. need a cheap compare-and-swap or sequence-based lease allocation in quota service. strong consistency for leases only, not for accounting.

sara: operational concerns: when we split enforcement (ingress) and fairness (serving), debugging becomes harder. we should emit correlated trace ids and three core metrics: denied_count, avg_route_latency, fairness_score per-tenant. also expose a route_decision_reason tag (quota|latency|fallback).

alex: agreed on metrics. minimal config that an operator can tune: burst_size, lease_ttl_ms, local_cache_ttl_ms, fallback_variant. sample policy YAML below: 

```
policy:
  ingress_enforcement: hard
  burst:
    type: lease
    lease_ttl_ms: 1500
    lease_window: 50
  serving_routing:
    priority: [latency_slo, cost, fairness_score]
    fallback_model: smaller-quantized
```

john: implementation tradeoffs:
- Option A: ingress synchronous check (RPC) to quota service per request -> accurate but adds latency and high QPS to quota service.
- Option B: ingress local-token-cache + background sync -> fast, slightly eventual, more complex.
- Option C: push enforcement to CDN/proxy layer (edge) -> reduces datacenter load but makes rollout + audits harder.
Which do we pick?

maya: we should start with Option B (local cache + lease for bursts) and instrument heavily. Option A is fallback only for critical tenants that buy strict SLO guarantees. Option C is longer-term; edge can be noisy for accounting.

lee: agree. if we go B, schedule a small perf test: 10k rps synthetic tenants, burst patterns, and measure false-allow and false-deny rates. Also test GC/partition recovery: what happens when quota-service leader restarts?

sara: also decide API surface between ingress and quota-service: we need two calls: check_and_reserve(tenant_id, units, mode) which can return {ok, lease_id, remaining} and release_lease(lease_id) for returned unused tokens. keep payload tiny (tenant, units, mode). prefer HTTP/2 gRPC for perf.

alex: agreed on API. pseudocode example: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://quota.service/check -d '{"tenant":"acct-42","units":32,"mode":"burst"}'
# -> {"ok":true,"lease_id":"L-123","remaining":120}
```

deploy-bot: deploy queued: quota-service v0.9.1 to staging at 1845001500 :rocket:

quota-bot: updated quota config for acct-42: monthly_limit=1e8, burst_limit=500, lease_ttl_ms=1500

john: one more safety pattern: add per-ingress backoff + token-sampling that probabilistically drops low-priority requests when queue depth grows. avoids thundering herd.

maya: good. concise action items:
- alex: write RFC appendix with API shapes and lease semantics (due EOD Fri).
- lee: perf test harness for Option B (start Mon).
- sara: define metrics + dashboards (denied_count, lease_conflict_rate, avg_decision_latency).
- john: prototype ingress local cache in the front proxy (two-week spike).

alex: thanks all — will open the PR after the RFC appendix. ping me in #oncall if you see quota-service errors. :handshake:
